subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a six-wheeled railgun carrier design—roughly 9 meters long, with deployed stabilizer outriggers and a rear turret mounting long forward-facing rails over the cab.

I'll add joints for the chassis root, wheels, outrigger legs, and turret yaw/pitch, keeping things to standard bone-driven parts using the clockwork kit's panelled and metal helpers. Now I'm working out the hull dimensions, wheel axle positions, and rail placement so the railgun sits angled slightly upward over the cab roof.

For the pitch rotation I'm figuring out the sign convention around the X axis so the barrel tips up rather than down, then applying the pose after the parts are built so they follow correctly. I'm also planning the four stabilizer outrigger legs positioned fore and aft along the hull.

For wheel-ground contact I'm placing the pads right at ground level with a slight sink so they read as braced against the surface. I'm also planning the texture work — hazard stripes, unit emblems, HUD screens, warning decals — plus panelled metal hull paint with countershading camo, and glow accents on the rail gap, headlights, and leg lights, before setting up small geometry helper functions for building the parts.

Now I'm detailing the leg and wheel assembly: tyre cylinders rotated to sit correctly, rims with hub bolts, spin joints per wheel, and a cab built from a sloped box to fake a windscreen. For the legs I'm defining joints and rod geometry from the hip to a hydraulic cylinder down to a flat foot pad, plus decal planes mapped onto the cab doors, aiming for a full build around two hundred lines including armour plates, a radar mast, light bar, and turret-side ammo drums.
